title: New license request: WordNet License
body:
### How license meets inclusion principles

This license was used by Princeton for [WordNet](https://wordnet.princeton.edu/). From their FAQ page, "WordNet® is a large lexical database of English. Nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs are grouped into sets of cognitive synonyms (synsets), each expressing a distinct concept." It is "freely and publicly available for download."

The license used by WordNet is similar to the CMU variant of MIT. Fedora considers it to be an [MIT variant](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Licensing:MIT#WordNet_Variant). It is more similar to CMU, but probably not similar enough to be handled with a regex.

title: New license request: FSFUL with short warranty disclaimer
body:
### How license meets inclusion principles

This appears to be a new variant of FSFULLR that adds a short warranty disclaimer. The disclaimer is the same as in FSFAP which is shorter than in FSFULLRWD. This variant replaced FSFULLR in Gnulib in October 2024 and thus it will appear in many packages that use Gnulib (coreutils, gettext, gzip, ...).

Gnulib commits that added the short warranty disclaimer:
* https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gnulib.git/commit/?id=b1f65faabbc86a539e469c4ebecce0619dedefe3
* https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gnulib.git/commit/?id=582eb499ca9a49d9f4e016b9e3f7f8f70d3036dc

There is a [mailing list thread](https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-gnulib/2024-10/msg00115.html) about this addition. The following two messages in the thread show that people were aware that this is a new license variant:

* https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-gnulib/2024-10/msg00124.html
* https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-gnulib/2024-10/msg00126.html

Gnulib has [one file](https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gnulib.git/tree/users.txt?id=7b08932179d0d6b017f7df01a2ddf6e096b038e3) that says "This file is free documentation" instead of "free software". Maybe it could make sense to match the pattern `(software|documentation)` in that sentence in case some day the text appears in some other file too.

A short identifier like FSFULLRSWD (FSF UL LR SWD) would have a style similar to the related licenses (FSFUL, FSFULLR, and FSFULLRWD). I suggest FSFUL-2024 because it looks more readable and also gives a hint which of these variants is the latest.

In Gnulib, the license text appears [as comment lines](https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gnulib.git/tree/etc/license-notices/unlimited?id=7b08932179d0d6b017f7df01a2ddf6e096b038e3) and [with a copyright notice](https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gnulib.git/tree/modules/COPYING?id=7b08932179d0d6b017f7df01a2ddf6e096b038e3) (the copyright years vary in the `.m4` files).

### License Name

FSF Unlimited License (with license retention and short warranty disclaimer)

### Suggested short identifier

FSFUL-2024

### License or Exception?

license

### URL to license text

https://git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gnulib.git/tree/etc/license-notices/unlimited?id=7b08932179d0d6b017f7df01a2ddf6e096b038e3

### OSI Status

Not Submitted

### License author or steward

Unknown

### URL to project(s) that use license

https://www.gnu.org/software/gnulib/

### paste text of license here

This file is free software; the Free Software Foundation
gives unlimited permission to copy and/or distribute it,
with or without modifications, as long as this notice is preserved.
This file is offered as-is, without any warranty.

title: libpng changes over the years
body:
see https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/issues/296

http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/src/libpng-LICENSE.txt is the URL for both `libpng-2.0` and `Libpng`

the first part/license:
- is a match to `libpng-2.0` (and this is the URL is referenced in the SPDX entry) which was added for version 3.5 in 2019

the second part/license:
- SPDX added https://spdx.org/licenses/Libpng.html in 2010 for version 1.4 of the SPDX License List (see https://lists.spdx.org/g/spdx/message/236?p=%2C%2C%2C20%2C0%2C0%2C0%3A%3Acreated%2C%2Clibpng%2C20%2C2%2C0%2C22079229 
- discussion of this at https://lists.spdx.org/g/spdx/topic/22079227#msg235
- SPDX added what existed on that same URL at that point in time. See https://web.archive.org/web/20101202114005/http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/src/libpng-LICENSE.txt

BUT over the years, various things were updated such as the list of names and references to version numbers (which would be replaceable by SPDX matching guidelines, but need markup added)
More substantial text changes occurred as well: 
- Feb 2016: https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/commit/f78d1cd47ad2fb26f8435b82bedc2470dc6ae357#diff-c693279643b8cd5d248172d9c22cb7cf4ed163a3c98c8a3f69c2717edd3eacb7
- Feb 2016: https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/commit/08bd7654bc15ee53a6f3c6199aedfab636027588#diff-c693279643b8cd5d248172d9c22cb7cf4ed163a3c98c8a3f69c2717edd3eacb7
- July 2018: https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/commit/c36c09f00426a07fef5c6d6a7361c12a47e6439b

`libpng-2.0` was added in Nov 2018, which also altered some of the text order, see https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/commit/e79085a1724ccc5526dc752f6a696b3a94ef8cfa

question is for SPDX now: should these various changes over the years be handled with markup or constitute a new license?

title: Classpath-exception-2.0 variant in Free Pascal
body:
During Fedora License review
  https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/issues/548
we found in package `fpc` (Free Pascal) an exception that is close to `Classpath-exception-2.0` and used in combination with LGPL-2.1-or-later.

This exception is identical to `Classpath-exception-2.0` except that it omits the first paragraph/sentence:

```
Linking this library statically or dynamically with other modules is making a combined work based on this library. Thus, the terms and conditions of the GNU General Public License version 2 cover the whole combination.
```

Should this section be marked as optional in current exception? Or this should be new id?


Full text of the license:
https://gitlab.com/freepascal.org/fpc/source/-/blob/release_3_2_2/rtl/COPYING.FPC

```
This is the file COPYING.FPC, it applies to the Free Pascal Run-Time Library 
(RTL) and packages (packages) distributed by members of the Free Pascal 
Development Team.

The source code of the Free Pascal Runtime Libraries and packages are 
distributed under the Library GNU General Public License 
(see the file COPYING) with the following modification:

As a special exception, the copyright holders of this library give you
permission to link this library with independent modules to produce an
executable, regardless of the license terms of these independent modules,
and to copy and distribute the resulting executable under terms of your choice,
provided that you also meet, for each linked independent module, the terms
and conditions of the license of that module. An independent module is a module
which is not derived from or based on this library. If you modify this
library, you may extend this exception to your version of the library, but you are
not obligated to do so. If you do not wish to do so, delete this exception
statement from your version.
```
